title: JAM Physics — Demo Mini Mock
subject: physics
description: A 13-question warm-up in the real exam interface. Use it to get used to the palette, the NAT keypad and the calculator before sitting a full paper.

sections.name: Section A
sections.instructions: Multiple Choice Questions. Each question has four options of which only one is correct. A wrong answer costs one third of the question's marks.

questions.prompt: For the position vector $\vec{r} = x\,\hat{i} + y\,\hat{j} + z\,\hat{k}$, the value of $\nabla \cdot \vec{r}$ is
questions.explanation: $\nabla \cdot \vec{r} = \partial x/\partial x + \partial y/\partial y + \partial z/\partial z = 3$.

questions.prompt: A particle in a one-dimensional infinite potential well of width $L$ has ground state energy $E_1$. The energy of its second excited state is
questions.explanation: $E_n = n^2 E_1$. The second excited state is $n = 3$, so $E_3 = 9E_1$.

questions.prompt: An ideal gas undergoes a reversible isothermal expansion. Which of the following quantities of the gas remains constant during the process?
questions.explanation: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, which is fixed. Entropy increases, pressure falls and volume rises.

questions.prompt: In the circuit shown, an ideal $12\ \text{V}$ battery is connected to a $4\ \Omega$ resistor in series with a parallel combination of $6\ \Omega$ and $3\ \Omega$ resistors. The current through the $3\ \Omega$ resistor is
questions.explanation: The parallel pair is $2\ \Omega$, so the total resistance is $6\ \Omega$ and the battery current is $2\ \text{A}$. The pair has $2 \times 2 = 4\ \text{V}$ across it, so the $3\ \Omega$ resistor carries $4/3\ \text{A}$.

questions.prompt: The eigenvalues of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$ are
questions.explanation: $(2-\lambda)^2 - 1 = 0$ gives $\lambda = 1, 3$. Check: the trace is $4$ and the determinant is $3$.

questions.prompt: An object is placed $30\ \text{cm}$ in front of a thin convex lens of focal length $20\ \text{cm}$. The image formed is
options: real, inverted and at $60\ \text{cm}$ from the lens
virtual, erect and at $60\ \text{cm}$ from the lens
real, inverted and at $12\ \text{cm}$ from the lens
virtual, erect and at $12\ \text{cm}$ from the lens
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{60}$ (object distance taken as a magnitude), so the image is real, $60\ \text{cm}$ beyond the lens, inverted and twice the size.

sections.name: Section B
sections.instructions: Multiple Select Questions. One or more options are correct. Full marks only for selecting all the correct options and no incorrect one. There is no negative marking and no partial marking.

questions.prompt: Which of the following operators, acting on square-integrable wavefunctions in one dimension, are Hermitian?
questions.explanation: $d/dx$ is anti-Hermitian: integrating by parts gives $\langle \phi | \psi' \rangle = -\langle \phi' | \psi \rangle$. Multiplying by $-i\hbar$ makes it Hermitian, and the square of a Hermitian operator is Hermitian.

questions.prompt: For a conservative force field $\vec{F}(\vec{r})$, which of the following statements are correct?
options: The work done by $\vec{F}$ around any closed path is zero
$\vec{F}$ can be written as $-\nabla V$ for some scalar function $V(\vec{r})$
The work done by $\vec{F}$ between two points depends on the path taken
questions.explanation: The first three are equivalent definitions of a conservative field. Path independence is exactly what the fourth statement denies.

questions.prompt: A series LCR circuit is driven by a sinusoidal source at its resonant frequency. Which of the following statements are correct?
options: The impedance of the circuit is minimum and equal to $R$
The current is in phase with the source voltage
The power factor of the circuit is zero
The voltages across $L$ and $C$ are equal in magnitude
questions.explanation: At resonance $X_L = X_C$, so the reactances cancel: $Z = R$, the phase angle is zero and the power factor is $1$, not $0$.

sections.name: Section C
sections.instructions: Numerical Answer Type questions. Enter the answer as a number using the keypad. There are no options and no negative marking.

questions.prompt: A radioactive sample has a half-life of $20$ minutes. The fraction of the original nuclei that remains undecayed after $60$ minutes is ________. (Give your answer as a decimal, to three decimal places.)
questions.explanation: Sixty minutes is three half-lives, so the fraction left is $(1/2)^3 = 0.125$.

questions.prompt: The number of degrees of freedom of a rigid diatomic molecule (vibration not excited) is ________.
questions.explanation: Three translational and two rotational. Rotation about the bond axis does not count.

questions.prompt: A simple pendulum of length $1.0\ \text{m}$ makes small oscillations where $g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$. Its time period, in seconds, is ________. (Round off to two decimal places.)

A block of mass $m$ slides down a frictionless plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal, as shown. Taking $g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$, the acceleration of the block, in $\text{m/s}^2$, is ________. (Round off to one decimal place.)
